nuevos.titulo_original: How to Stop Waking Up to Pee At Night
nuevos.descripcion:
If you’re dealing with frequent urination at night, the problem is not your bladder.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4xPOE4t

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Approximately 1 in 5 men and 1 in 4 women in the U.S. get up at least once or twice to urinate every night. Waking up to pee, even just once, can wreck your sleep and wreak havoc on your health!

So what’s really causing this widespread issue? The antidiuretic hormone (ADH) plays a crucial role in preventing excessive urination. A problem with this hormone affects water balance, causing you to produce more urine, especially at night.

Too much salt and not enough potassium, blood sugar issues, and insulin resistance all affect ADH and can cause you to produce more urine to eliminate excess salt and sugar.

nuevos.titulo_original: The MOST Dangerous Carbs in the World!
nuevos.descripcion:
The most dangerous carbs are highly refined starches that break down rapidly into glucose and can spike blood sugar and insulin more than actual sugar. 

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3VoI33B

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Watch for these common forms of industrial starch:

* Maltodextrin
* Modified food starch
* Cornstarch
* Tapioca starch
* Wheat starch
* Refined rice flour

These ingredients are commonly used in processed foods and can be easy to overlook because they aren’t always labeled as sugar.

nuevos.titulo_original: The 7 Signs Your Liver is Dying
nuevos.descripcion:
Waking up between 2 and 3 a.m., experiencing right shoulder pain, bruising easily, or dealing with brain fog could be signs that your liver needs attention.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/46WQB4c

Other potential warning signs include:

• Waking up between 2 and 3 a.m.
• Right shoulder pain
• Bruising easily
• Itching at night
• Low tolerance to alcohol
• Fat accumulation around the belly with skinny legs
• Irritability, temper issues, brain fog, and difficulty focusing

These symptoms can have many possible causes and don't necessarily mean you have liver disease. However, recognizing changes in your body and understanding how they may relate to liver health can help you know when it's worth seeking medical advice.

Discover the warning signs to watch for and learn more about supporting healthy liver function.
